newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply off, gold rattled.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply off, gold rattled.

text.p: New York precious metals ended sharply weaker Friday, the losses coming hard on the heels of Germany's plan to reevaluate the Bundesbank's gold reserves, rattling yellow metal sentiment despite denials that not a single ounce of the central bank's hoard would be sold.
"If the market hears central bank and gold in the same sentence, it gets severely rattled," Dinsa Mehta, Chase Manhattan's chief bullion dealer, said.
COMEX June gold ended $3.50 lower at $344.90 an ounce, traded $347.90 to $344.30. Bullion was quoted mid-afternoon at $343.80/$344.30.

Thursday, Germany's Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Bundesbank reserves would be reevaluated but none sold. This would help Germany qualify for European economic and monetary union by generating windfall profits.

Greg Drury of Mitsui USA said that a leading central bank was looking at its reserves tended to have a negative effect on gold. "Central banks tend to be net sellers these days and people, rightly or wrongly, jump to conclusions," Drury said.
The failure of precious metals to sustain their rallies, was also noted by many dealers as a negative factor.
"The truth of the matter is that gold is getting demonetized and demystified and this is taking out some of its underpinning," Mehta said.
The Bundesbank is one of the last central banks to reevaluate its gold reserves to bring them up to current market value.

The downward spiral began with selling in silver, whose trading range had become narrow, leading to an inevitable breakout, dealers said. Gold then took the lead to push the precious metals complex lower as the platinum group metals, which had hitherto injected buoyancy into the complex, ran out of steam.
"The market for platinum looks overextended on the upside and maybe some people in the silver market were a bit nervous about that," Drury said.
He expected gold and silver spot prices to test $340.00 and $4.60, respectively.
COMEX July silver settled 16.5 cents lower at $4.693, traded $4.85 to $4.665.
Volume in gold and silver were overly heavy at 40,000 and 26,000 lots, respectively.
Platinum and palladium were still largely in a holding pattern, waiting for Russia's 1997 exports to begin moving, but the losses in gold and silver were enough to drag prices down, dealers said.
July NYMEX platinum settled $2.70 lower at $391.20, traded $393.50 to $389.50. June NYMEX palladium went out $1.15 lower at $172.10.
Monday, Johnson Matthey will release its platinum group metals annual report.
The precious metals market will also be looking to see if U.S. interest rates are changed following the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday.
